$comment: Assets owned by gems that expect a Rails asset pipeline, mapped into our esbuild build.
Read by esbuild.config.js and by test/assets/asset_mappings_test.rb, so neither side
has to know anything about the other. The only runtime link between Ruby and JS is the
`bundle info <gem> --path` call esbuild makes to locate each gem.
The two lists answer different questions, so they do not line up one to one.
assetPaths is where a gem's assets can be *found*. It mirrors what the gem pushes into
`config.assets.paths`, is asserted against the real registration by the audit test, and is
the space the esbuild resolver searches when a gem's own stylesheet references something
by logical path. Paths are relative to the gem root.
manifestEntries is what has to be *addressable from Ruby*, and so needs a manifest key. An
asset earns one only if Ruby names it. Assets reached from inside a gem's own CSS or JS
arrive through assetPaths instead, and assets read straight off disk need neither.
`logicalName` is the name Ruby passes to a helper, minus the extension; a `*` in it is
replaced by the matched file's basename. These are the gem's own logical names, the way
Propshaft would resolve them — `avo/logo` for `image_tag "avo/logo.png"`. precompiled_assets
looks under `images/` first for typed helpers and falls back to the undecorated name, so one
entry per asset answers both typed and untyped lookups.
Known limitation: the audit only sees what a gem registers explicitly. Propshaft also adds
every engine's app/assets/* children implicitly; assets relying on that (Avo's empty
avo-overrides files) are not covered here. We ship our own avo-overrides instead.

assetPaths.$comment: Avo's own prebuilt CSS and JS. Gives them the logical names its layout asks for, e.g. avo/application.css.

$comment: Logos and favicons — and the root that resolves Avo's webfonts. Its stylesheet has the
logical name avo/application.css, so a `url(fonts/inter-…)` inside it means the logical
path avo/fonts/inter-…, which lives here. That is why the built font is emitted as
avo--avo-fonts-inter-… : the flattened logical path.
Icons that avo-icons inlines into the HTML, reading them off disk through its own
Avo::Icons.configuration.custom_paths. They are never fetched over HTTP, so they get no
manifestEntries — one would emit 49 digested files nothing ever requests.
Registered by Avo so the bare logical name fonts/inter-… resolves, the way Sprockets
would. Propshaft reaches the fonts through app/assets/images instead, and so do we, so
nothing actually resolves through this one. It is listed because the audit test asserts
equality with what Avo registers, not with what we happen to use.
Named by Avo's layout: stylesheet_link_tag "avo/dependencies" and "avo/application",
javascript_include_tag "avo/application", and "avo/late-registration" from
Avo::AssetManager::JavascriptComponent. avo.custom.js is built too and goes unreferenced;
only importmap apps link it, via Avo's install generator.
Named by Avo's appearance defaults, e.g. image_tag "avo/logo.png" and the favicons its
_appearance partial reaches for. The webfonts one directory down are deliberately absent:
the stylesheet above already pulls them in, and an entry here would emit them a second time.
